correctness.rationale: For any compatible set J of forced UD step positions, deletion/insertion of all prescribed peaks is bijective with Dyck paths of semilength n-|J|. Character expansion gives a sum over independent subsets J weighted (-2)^|J| C_{n-|J|}. Legendre yields v2(C_m)=s2(m+1)-1. The binary digit-sum inequality is strict for nonempty J at odd n, proving each Walsh multiplier congruent to C_n modulo 2^{s2(n+1)}, so none vanishes. Lagrange inversion derives symmetric Narayana numbers, whose alternating sum is zero when n is even. All boundary cases n>=1 are covered. Independent integer enumeration and FWT check n<=10; all formula identities n<=8 and contraction counts at n=6 are verified by verify.py. No finite check is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The novel assessed statement is uniform exact 2-adic valuation of all Fourier characters for odd Dyck semilength, and complete odd/even invertibility of the peak-position counting convolution. Classical Narayana symmetry already covers only the even-order all-selected zero. Peak-height enumeration, one-half positional-descent refinements, and up-step incidence Fourier transforms do not state or imply the all-position peak-character congruence. Searches and literature comparison are bounded and do not certify historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: A complete infinite-family convolution invertibility classification and exact full-spectrum 2-adic rigidity on a canonical Catalan statistic are mathematically motivated. It distinguishes even Catalan totals that nevertheless yield a zero-free Fourier transform, and quantifies determinant divisibility and reversible peak-profile counting. The essential uniform arithmetic law is not a single finite-table entry or a routine restatement of Narayana symmetry; no universal sharp gap or even nullity is overclaimed.
